🇾🇪⚔️ Houthis launch surprise blitz offensive along key coastal highway, seize areas just 80km west of Aden
 
Yemen’s Ansar Allah-aligned Armed Forces have advanced 65km+ along the strategic Aden-Hodeidah Coastal Road in Lahij governorate over the past 24 hours, liberating the towns of Dar Am Umayrah and Khour al-Umayrah, and trapping enemy fighters in the areas of Al Suqayyah and Ras al-Arah, giving them the option to surrender or withdraw without their weapons.
OSINT reporting also indicates an advance on Ghayl al-Barir, Huwayrib and the Kharaz military camp, with Ansar Allah looking poised to pocket enemy forces to the west in areas including Ash Shuqayrah.
Saudi jets have sought to stem the offensive by launching dozens of airstrikes.
👉 Houthi politburo member Mohammad al-Farah said the advance in Lahij has caused disarray among enemy forces. Reports suggest one local commander abandoned the front and retreated, and that Mahmoud al-Subaihi, a senior member of the Saudi-backed Presidential Leadership Council (PLC), has left Aden for Riyadh.
The coastal advance has driven enemy forces further from Bab al-Mandab, which they previously vowed to retake, and threatens to become the biggest rout for Aden government troops since the Houthis’ surprise offensive on [Mokha](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74962) and the southern Red Sea coast in September, and [the encirclement of the strategic city of Taiz](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77545) several weeks later.

🇺🇸❗️ Rights groups urge Congress to hold Hegseth accountable for Yemeni civilian casualties
Twelve US, British and Yemeni rights and civilian protection nonprofits have signed a joint appeal expressing “alarm at the extent of US-caused civilian deaths and injuries in Yemen during last year’s bombing campaign,” and calling for “rigorous congressional oversight” to bring the DoD to account.
Citing the military’s own estimates on civilian casualties during Operation Rough Rider, including nearly 400 deaths and injuries across just three attacks on Sanaa, Ras Isa and Saada in April 2025, the appeal pointed out that a year-and-a-half later, 15 additional incidents officially remain[ “under assessment.”](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/60400)
🔊 “The Department’s failure to reckon with and learn from the harms of Operation Rough Rider may be seen in their actions in the opening days of the war between the US, Israel, and Iran, in which the United States and Israel reportedly killed and injured thousands of civilians – including over 100 children in[ a school in Minab](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77588),” the letter said.
The groups urged lawmakers to review the DoD’s conclusions that formal apologies and compensation for civilian deaths were not warranted.
The appeal was signed by major US-based organizations like Amnesty and Human Rights Watch, as well as Mwatana for Human Rights, a Saana-based war monitoring group.
👉 This week, Secretary Hegseth narrowly survived[ a resolution](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77597) by outgoing Rep. Thomas Massie to have him impeached on abuse of power, high crimes and misdemeanors charges over Iran, the “unlawful war in Yemen,” extrajudicial killings in the Caribbean, and the kidnapping of Venezuela’s president.
Rough Rider was the Trump administration’s attempt to make up for President Biden’s failed bombing operation against Yemen. Both intended to degrade Ansar Allah’s ability to enforce its blockade of the Red Sea, and launch missile and drone attacks into Israel in solidarity with Gaza. Neither succeeded.

☢️ Nuclear explosion in space could disable 98% of satellites within days
Researchers from the University of Wisconsin–Madison and Princeton University modeled the consequences of a hypothetical 1-megaton nuclear explosion at an altitude of 500 km above Earth. Their simulation found that the resulting radiation belt could disable around 98% of satellites in low Earth orbit within a week, with damaging effects potentially lasting for years.
The findings come amid growing geopolitical tensions over the militarization of space. Russia and Belarus have jointly opposed the deployment of weapons of any kind in orbit and attempts to use space for military confrontation, including through US President Donald Trump's proposed Golden Dome missile defense system, which envisages space-based interceptors.
The study highlights the potential consequences of nuclear escalation in orbit, where a single detonation could threaten civilian, commercial, and military satellite infrastructure worldwide.
